persona: Stressed and venting after a bad week; calms down when asked clear questions. Lodged a windscreen claim two days before this accident and explains the difference if asked.
initial_message: Honestly, what a week!! On Tuesday morning (the 15th) I was backing out of the carport in the pouring rain and hit the steel post!! The back left corner of my car is all pushed in, the tail light is cracked and the panel above the wheel is dented. And this is only two days after a stone cracked my windscreen on the highway, I can't believe it. Nobody's hurt, the car still drives, I'm just so over it. What do I do now?

facts.incident.cause: Turned too early while reversing out of the carport in heavy rain

facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the back left corner, taken in the rain. Available now.

facts.if_asked_about_other_claims: Yes, I lodged a windscreen claim on Monday the 14th, for a stone that cracked it on State Highway 1 on Sunday the 13th. That is a different thing; the windscreen has nothing to do with the carport.

Wet concrete, grey morning light. The frame shows only the tail light, the rear quarter panel, the bumper corner and the rear wheel. No text, no logos, no people.

design.notes: Possible duplicate by date only: the earlier motor claim (windscreen, incident 13 September 2026) is a different event two days before this one. The check compares family and dates, so it fires; staff decide. It is not counted as a prior claim. The quote is over NZD 5,000.

triage.rationale: Single vehicle in the claimant's own carport, nobody hurt, car drivable, a photo and a complete quote. The quote total, NZD 5,773.00 including GST, is over NZD 5,000. Another submitted motor claim from the same account has an incident two days earlier (13 September 2026), so the possible-duplicate check fires even though the claimant describes a different event; staff decide. It is not a fraud indicator. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: No receipt or ownership document in the pack

prior_claims_12m.basis: The only earlier claim is the possible duplicate, which is not counted again

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (15 May 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2024-05-15, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.

possible_duplicate.basis: Another submitted motor claim from the same account, incident 13 September 2026, two days before 15 September 2026
